classes.name: Избори за народни представители в Народното събрание
classes.finest_note: Votes are published by polling section (секция); section areas are lists of streets and addresses, not mapped. Votes cast abroad are counted in sections outside the country and allocated nationally.
classes.note: 240 members for four years (Constitution arts. 63–64). List PR with preference votes in 31 multi-member constituencies (МИР), seats shared nationally by the Hare–Niemeyer method among lists over 4% and then to constituencies; 2009 used 209 PR seats plus 31 single-member districts. Many early elections since 2013, after failed government formation (Constitution art. 99).

cadence.vacancy_rule: A seat that falls vacant passes to the next candidate on the same list in the same constituency (Изборен кодекс); a dissolved Assembly is followed by an early election within two months (Constitution art. 99).

classes.name: Избори за Велико Народно събрание
classes.note: 400 members. The 7th Grand National Assembly, elected in June 1990 under the 1971 Constitution as amended (200 seats in single-member districts in two rounds and 200 by list PR in 28 constituencies), adopted the 1991 Constitution. The 1991 Constitution (arts. 157–163) keeps the Grand National Assembly for a new constitution, territorial changes, and certain amendments; none has been elected since.

dates.note: First round: 200 single-member districts and 200 list seats.
Second round in single-member districts with no majority winner.

access.evidence: Results notices of the central election commission of 1990 are in the State Gazette; no machine-readable official return was found.

classes.name: Избори за президент и вицепрезидент на републиката
classes.finest_note: Polling-section protocols from 2016 in the open data; the President and Vice President run on one ticket.
classes.note: Direct election of the President and Vice President on one ticket for five years, at most two terms (Constitution arts. 92–95). The first President, Zhelyu Zhelev, was chosen by the Grand National Assembly in 1990 (see nepreki_izbori).

cadence.runoff_rule: Elected in the first round with more than half of the valid votes if more than half of the voters on the rolls voted; otherwise the top two meet seven days later and the one with more votes wins (Constitution art. 93).
cadence.vacancy_rule: The Vice President serves out the term (Constitution art. 97).

classes.note: Held only in mayoralties that meet the population bar on the day the decree calling the election is published: 350 residents under the Act on Administrative-Territorial Division art. 16 item 1 (Electoral Code 2011, § 16 of the transitional provisions), and more than 100 residents by permanent address under § 17 of the transitional provisions of the 2014 Electoral Code. Smaller places get an appointed deputy mayor (кметски наместник). So the elected count is below the register's 3,041 kmetstva, and contest counts come from the CIK's own per-election files (a mayoralty counts when it has a protocol or a candidate in the file).

classes.name_en: National Assembly elections of the Principality and Kingdom
classes.note: Ordinary and Grand National Assemblies under the Tarnovo Constitution, from the first ordinary Assembly in 1879 to the 25th in 1945, by majority and later PR systems that changed many times. Results are in the State Gazette and the statistical yearbooks.

dates.quote: Сформира се непосредствено след първите парламентарни избори в Българското княжество проведени на 30 септември и 7 октомври 1879 г.
dates.note: I Ordinary National Assembly. Second round 7 October 1879; seat count not settled by the sources read. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: проведени на 13 и 20 януари 1880 г.
dates.note: II Ordinary National Assembly. Second round 20 January 1880; seat count not settled by the sources read. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: се провеждат на 14 и 21 юни (27 юни и 4 юли – нов стил) същата година
dates.note: II Grand National Assembly, Svishtov. Second round 21 June 1881; 307 deputies attended. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: се провеждат на 21 ноември
dates.note: III Ordinary National Assembly. The law cut the membership to 47; supplementary elections in summer 1883 raised it to 55. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Парламентарните избори се провеждат на 27 май и 3 юни същата година
dates.note: IV Ordinary National Assembly. Second round 3 June 1884; 195 deputies elected, joined by 91 from Eastern Rumelia in 1886. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: населението на Източна Румелия избира свои 91 народни представители на 11 и 18 май 1886
dates.note: Elections in Eastern Rumelia after the Unification for 91 deputies who joined the IV Ordinary National Assembly. Second round 18 May 1886. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: провеждат парламентарните избори на 28 септември 1886 г.
dates.note: III Grand National Assembly. 493 deputies elected; the vote failed in 7 of 85 electoral districts. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Провеждат се на 9 октомври същата година
dates.note: V Ordinary National Assembly. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: се провеждат на 26 август 1890 г.
dates.note: VI Ordinary National Assembly, convened 15 October 1890; decree of 14 June 1890. Seat count per the Assembly's chronology: 276. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Парламентарните избори се провеждат на 18 април същата година
dates.note: IV Grand National Assembly, Tarnovo. Seat count per the Assembly's chronology: 577. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Провеждат са на 18 юли (31 юли – нов стил) същата година
dates.note: VII Ordinary National Assembly, after the constitutional amendment of May 1893 cut the ratio to one deputy per 20,000. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Провеждат са на 10 септември същата година
dates.note: VIII Ordinary National Assembly. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.quote: Провеждат се на 17 ноември същата година
dates.note: IX Ordinary National Assembly. Date as printed in the decree and the press of the day (Julian calendar); dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

dates.note: XV Ordinary National Assembly: 170 seats by majority and 43 by PR in Plovdiv and Tarnovo, 213 in all. Date as printed in the yearbook; dates before 1916 are not converted to the Gregorian calendar.

access.evidence: Results by district in State Gazette notices and the statistical yearbooks of the Kingdom.
Statistical yearbooks with a table of each legislative election from 1899, and volumes of election statistics by district for the X–XXI Ordinary and V Grand National Assemblies (1899–1927).

classes.name: Непреки избори
classes.disposition_reason: Officers chosen by elected bodies: the Prime Minister and the chair of the National Assembly by the Assembly, the President by the Grand National Assembly in 1990, Constitutional Court and Supreme Judicial Council members partly by the Assembly, and council chairs by municipal councils; no electorate votes.

classes.name: Съдебна власт
classes.disposition_reason: No judge, prosecutor, or police officer is elected by voters: judges are appointed by the Supreme Judicial Council (Constitution art. 129), and lay judges are chosen by municipal councils and general assemblies of courts.

classes.name: Издигане на кандидати
classes.disposition_reason: No state-run primaries: parties, coalitions, and initiative committees nominate candidates by their own rules and register them with the election commissions (Изборен кодекс); there is no public nominating vote.

classes.name: Нетериториални избори
classes.disposition_reason: Bulgaria has no minority rolls, reserved communal seats, or other non-territorial electorates; elections inside professional chambers, universities, and trade unions are private and run by those bodies.
